Self Pickup, now on Cart

60% of prepaid users order through Cart, but pickup only lived on Buy Now. We’re bringing the same pickup card to the Cart’s Review step.

01 — Why Cart

Most prepaid orders come through Cart, and Cart had no pickup

Self Pickup is live for prepaid users near partner stores, but only on the Buy Now path. Most of the buyers who could pick up never saw the option.

60% of prepaid users place their order via Cart.

TODO: data source and period for the 60%
02 — Today on Cart

Today, Cart has no option to do Self Pickup

Cart → Review → Payment. The buyer checks every item on step 1, then sees the address and the same items again on step 2. There’s no slot for pickup anywhere in the flow.

The pickup card lands on step 2, alongside the delivery address that already lives there.

03 — Today on Buy Now

How Self Pickup looks on Buy Now today

This is the steady state we’re carrying over to Cart. Home stays pre-selected; the pickup card earns attention with a discount band.

Buy Now also has two FTUX variants. Cart takes only the steady state. The price strike inside the card never animates.

04 — Pickup discount

₹30 base plus ₹10 for every unit in the order

Pickup discount₹30 base + ₹10 × XX = total quantity in the order. It counts units, so 2 of the same item and 2 different items both make X = 2.
Buy Now · 1 item → ₹40 OFF₹30 + ₹10 × 1. Matches the “₹40 OFF” band on Buy Now.
Cart · 3 items → ₹60 OFF₹30 + ₹10 × 3. Matches the “₹60 OFF” band in the Cart designs (bottles, kurti, diaper).
Cart · 1 item × qty 2 → ₹50 OFF₹30 + ₹10 × 2. The same item twice counts as 2.
05 — How we’re thinking about Cart

Same pickup pattern as Buy Now, placed for a multi-item checkout

We reuse the Buy Now pattern on purpose: the same card, discount band and motion, so buyers who’ve seen pickup on Buy Now recognise it on Cart. What changes is placement. Cart → Review → Payment: buyers check every item on step 1, then take a few into checkout (median 2 items at review cart, down from 4). By Review, the open question is how the order reaches them, so the delivery choice goes first and the items follow.

Same pattern, carried overCard, band, FTUX and steady-state motion all match Buy Now, so the understanding built there continues on Cart.
Items were seen one step agoStep 1 is the Cart itself: every item, size, quantity and price. Repeating them first on step 2 asks the buyer to re-read what they just checked.
Step 2 has one new decisionThe only new thing on Review is how the order reaches you. That decision goes first.
Cart lists are longBuy Now has one compact product row above delivery. A cart has three or more full item rows; above the delivery choice they’d push the pickup card down by the height of every item.
The saving grows with the cartPickup takes ₹30 + ₹10 × quantity off, so a bigger cart sees a bigger reason to pick up.
One cart, several delivery daysMulti-item carts are 83.6% of orders and their items land about 1.8 days apart, which shapes what comes next (see Next steps).
06 — Final design

Same pickup card, now on Cart’s Review step

First visit gets the FTUX. After that, the steady state plays on every landing on Review, with no quota and no dim: 2.0s, then the card rests green with its discount band.

08 — Next steps

Next: one pickup for the whole cart

Collect everything in one tripExperiment with telling users explicitly to collect once all their orders have reached the store. In a few LODs, users who order many items for store pickup already wait and collect them together.
Test a 3–7 day gap between deliveriesExperiment with the delta between delivery days in the 3–7 day range.
Stores hold orders for 7 daysThe F&E team is expanding how long stores keep an order to 7 days, so items that land days apart can wait for one pickup.
